current_task: EBOOK GENERATOR RECOVERY SPRINT: manuscript-stage root cause found and fixed, pending the owner's live re-test. Factory v1.7.7, commit 8961ac8, pushed to origin/main. After the v1.7.6 Resume Build fix, the owner's live re-test of "Container Gardening for Beginners" still failed the manuscript stage every time (including two Resume Build clicks), and the owner supplied the exact Render traceback: urllib.error.URLError: Connection refused, from services/ebook.py::generate_one_chapter. ROOT CAUSE: services/ai_providers.py's Local Manuscript Pilot (added 2026-09-03, ec9d3ee, long before this recovery sprint) routes chapter generation to a local Ollama engine at 127.0.0.1:11434 by default, unless FACTORY_AI_POLICY=premium. The owner set that variable on Render and redeployed; the failure persisted anyway -- the routing logic itself is correct and already proven by tests/test_ai_providers.py, so the gap is architectural: nothing in the hosted runtime ever REQUIRED that one custom variable to be right, and app.py's load_dotenv runs with override=True in production (the same failure shape that already bit TAVILY_API_KEY once, on 2026-08-29). FIX: routes_local() now also checks Render's own auto-injected RENDER variable and refuses local routing unconditionally when present, independent of FACTORY_AI_POLICY. Local development (RENDER unset) is completely unaffected. Full Release Gate: 2863 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 paid API calls. Fast Gate: 160 passed, 698 subtests. No LOCKED function was touched (services/ai_providers.py and services/ebook.py are not shared with word_search/crossword/coloring_book/invite_protection), so none were unlocked -- only ebook's PROTECTED registry entry gained these two files as declared dependencies. STILL OPEN: I cannot perform the actual live re-test myself -- no invite code / customer session in this environment. The owner must re-run "Container Gardening for Beginners" on the live site; success means the build advances past 30% into visuals/cover/design and ultimately reaches export-ready. Upgrade 2 still requires the owner's explicit approval and is not started by this fix.
